structured_output.hypothesis: Ecoregions that share the same climate-defined biome (mediterranean-type, ~25–35°S) fall into multiple, distinct biogeographic realms (defined by taxonomic composition), so climate does not determine biotic similarity.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Among the ecoregions of Biome 12 (Mediterranean Forests, Woodlands and Scrub), the Australian (southwest/south Australia), South African (Cape/fynbos) and central Chilean ecoregions are assigned to three different realms (Australasia, Afrotropic, Neotropic), and the biome spans at least 4 of the 8 realms. Also, the share of biomes (of 14) occurring in at least 3 realms is at least 50%.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The Australian, South African and Chilean Biome 12 ecoregions fall into 2 or fewer distinct realms, or Biome 12 spans 3 or fewer realms, or fewer than 50% of biomes occur in at least 3 realms (i.e., biome/climate largely predicts realm).
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'climatal and other physical conditions' is mapped to WWF biome (a climate/vegetation-structure class; the mediterranean biome is the modern analogue of his 25°–35° S example). 'Faunas and floras' similarity or dissimilarity is mapped to biogeographic realm, which Olson et al. define from taxonomic (family/genus-level) affinities. This is a coarse proxy and partly circular, since realms were drawn from taxon distributions, but it measures the claim's core: same physical conditions, different biotas. The test covers the 'dissimilarity' half (similar climates, different biotas); similarity-despite-different-climate is a secondary check via biomes within a realm. Nuance: biomes are not identical to Darwin's latitude bands.

dataset.publisher: World Wildlife Fund (WWF-US), hosted on USGS ScienceBase
dataset.why_it_fits: Shapefile wwf_terr_ecos (.shp/.dbf) of 825 terrestrial ecoregions nested in 14 biomes and 8 realms. The .dbf is expected to hold realm, biome and ecoregion-name fields (not listed on the landing page; to be confirmed from the .dbf or .shp.xml). Cross-tabulating biome by realm, with Biome 12 as the focus, directly tests whether the same climate class hosts different biotas.
